title: fix(test-env): keep the storage instrument from going blind on Node 26
body:
Fixes #7271

Every number below was measured on this branch in this run, at `aac3322e0` unless a
reading is explicitly labelled "before". Node 26.7.0 is a local toolchain download; the
container ships 20/21/22 only. CI stays pinned at 22.x — nothing here changes `ci.yml`.

## Root cause, measured

Node 22.22.2 has **no** Web Storage globals at all (`typeof Storage`, `typeof
localStorage`, `typeof sessionStorage` all `undefined`; `--experimental-webstorage`
turns them on). Node 26.7.0 has them **by default**: `Storage` is a function whose
constructor answers `Illegal constructor`, `sessionStorage` is a live native store, and
`localStorage` is a getter that warns `localStorage is not available because
--localstorage-file was not provided` and answers `undefined`.

Vitest's `populateGlobal` (v4.1.10, `dist/chunks/index.DC7d2Pf8.js`) decides per key:

```js
if (k in global) return keysArray.includes(k);   // keysArray = its hardcoded KEYS
```

`"Storage"` is on that list. `"localStorage"` and `"sessionStorage"` are not — grepped in
all three installed copies: 1 hit, 0 hits, 0 hits. So on Node 26, inside a happy-dom
environment, the class is copied from happy-dom while the two stores are left as Node's.
Measured with no setup file at all, happy-dom, v26.7.0:

| global | ctor | `instanceof globalThis.Storage` |
|---|---|---|
| `localStorage` | `undefined` (Node's warning getter) | false |
| `sessionStorage` | a class also named `Storage` (Node's) | **false** |

A `Storage.prototype` patch therefore observes **0** writes there, against 2 on Node 22.
The old shim in `vitest.setup.base.ts` only replaced a store that was missing or lacked
`clear`/`removeItem`: that caught `localStorage` (replaced with a plain object literal)
and **left `sessionStorage` as Node's**, which is the store the code under test writes.

## What changes

`vitest.setup.base.ts` states the rule positively — in a DOM environment every storage
global is that environment's own `Storage` — discriminating happy-dom's class from Node's
by constructibility (`new Storage()` throws `Illegal constructor` on Node's; happy-dom's
does not), and then **verifies it by identity** so that a future divergence fails by name
in every suite instead of one suite quietly measuring a store nobody wrote to.

`anonSeedScope-5746.enumeration.test.tsx` gains an environment guard that names this
failure mode **before** the ledger is consulted. It does not replace S0.

## The property the repair had to preserve, and the proof it does

S0 is the file's counter-probe; the whole point of the card is that a repair which makes
S1..S6 green while disarming S0 is worse than the bug. Two deliberate blindings on the
**repaired** tree, both of which the two guards accept (`instanceof` still holds), both
with the mutation confirmed on disk by blob hash and restored under a trap:

| ablation | node 22 | node 26 |
|---|---|---|
| E1 — merely READ the stores' methods in setup (happy-dom's proxy then hands out a bound method that a later `Storage.prototype` patch cannot reach) | 7 failed | 7 failed |
| E2 — pin the stores' methods as own properties | 7 failed | 7 failed |
| control — no ablation | 7 passed | 7 passed |

In both ablations neither guard fires and the failure is S0's own:

```
FAIL  S0 counter-probe — the instrument can see a write that is known to happen
AssertionError: expected 0 to be greater than 0
  anonSeedScope-5746.enumeration.test.tsx:356  expect(writes().length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
```

In the control the string `expected 0 to be greater than 0` is absent. E1 also reproduces
the claim the code comment makes about a four-method liveness probe.

## Readings on both Node versions, before and after

Same tree, one file swapped at a time, each swap confirmed by blob hash:

| condition | target suite, node 22 | target suite, node 26 |
|---|---|---|
| both files before | 7 passed | **7 failed** |
| both files after | 7 passed | 7 passed |
| new setup + old test | 7 passed | 7 passed |
| old setup + new test | 7 passed | 7 failed, and the guard names it: ``test environment: `sessionStorage` is not an instance …`` |

The third row is the honest one: the setup repair alone is what turns the suite green. The
test-file guard buys a named diagnosis at a later checkpoint, not the green.

## Blast radius of `vitest.setup.base.ts`

This file runs for every test in the repository, so the claim is not "it looks local". The
population is enumerated rather than sampled: the storage block branches on the
**environment**, not on the test file, and the farm has exactly two — `node` (the `unit`
project) and `happy-dom` (`dom`, `dom-heavy`, `dist`, `apps/console`). All four cells were
probed directly, before and after:

| env | node 22 before → after | node 26 before → after |
|---|---|---|
| happy-dom | identical: `instanceof` true, prototype patch observes 2 writes, `Object.keys` shows entries | broken → repaired |
| node (`unit`) | identical: in-memory shim for both stores | `sessionStorage` was Node's native store, now the same deterministic shim |

On the Node version CI pins, **both** environments read identically before and after: on
Node 22 nothing exists to displace happy-dom's stores, so the block's replacing branch is
never taken either way.

Named population, run end to end: the **102** test files that reference `localStorage`,
`sessionStorage` or `Storage` (`git grep -l` over `packages/`, `apps/`, `examples/`,
`scripts/`; list in the report).

| run | result |
|---|---|
| 102 files, node 22, before | 102 files / 1240 tests passed |
| 102 files, node 22, after | 102 files / 1240 tests passed |
| 102 files, node 26, before | **3 files / 12 tests failed** |
| 102 files, node 26, after | 102 files / 1240 tests passed |
| union at `aac3322e0`, node 22 and node 26 | 102 files / 1240 tests passed, both |

**Lit control.** A one-line mutation forcing that block down its replacing branch with the
plain-object shim, on node 22, turns **5 of the 102 files / 15 tests red** — so the
before/after equality above is a live measurement, not a dark one. Broader sample on the
repaired tree, node 22: `vitest run --shard=1/8`, 319 files / 3905 tests, all passed.

## The sibling, and the census

The sibling reported on the card, `packages/auth/src/__tests__/signOut-client-cache-purge-5198.test.tsx`
case 5777, reproduces on Node 26 before (1 failed) and is green after — **with no change
to that file**, because the repair is in the shared environment. Carrying a second edit
into `packages/auth` would have been redundant. A third suite nobody had reported,
`packages/auth/src/__tests__/sessionUserChangePurge-5664.test.tsx` (4 tests), behaves the
same way.

Four suites instrument `Storage.prototype` directly. Two of them stayed **green** on Node
26 before the repair, while the instrument was proven blind — i.e. they were passing
vacuously, which is exactly the hazard this card is about. Adding a temporary counter-probe
to each made them fail there, and one of them fails its counter-probe on Node 22 as well.
Neither carries a counter-probe of its own, so nothing would have said so. That is filed
separately rather than repaired here; it is a different fix (add counter-probes) in two
packages this card does not reach.

## What was not run locally

The full farm (2547 test files) was not run: one eighth of it holds the shared verify lock
for ~7.5 minutes on this box, so both a before and an after pass would have cost about two
hours of exclusive lock and starved the other agents. The narrowing is declared, not
silent: what ran is the enumerated environment matrix, the named 102-file population on
both Node versions before and after with a lit control, one eighth of the farm on the
repaired tree, and the gate family below. CI runs the farm exactly once regardless.

Gates, all green at `aac3322e0`: `check-changeset-presence` (it names the empty frontmatter
as the explicit exemption), `check-changeset-no-major`, `check:control-bytes`,
`check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `type-check:vitest-setup`,
`lint:coverage`, `type-check:coverage`, `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check`
(the edited test file confirmed present in `tsc --listFiles`). ESLint was run scoped to the
two edited files rather than repo-wide: 2 files linted per `--format json`, 0 errors, 2
pre-existing `no-explicit-any` warnings on untouched lines 37-38, and the config declares
no type-aware linting, so no untouched file's verdict can move.
